claim: ERS-002 promises 'blind adjudication', but nothing in the ledger, the evidence shard or ERS-013 establishes or requires blinding; ERS-013, the unit that fixes adjudication truthfulness, only requires that the adjudicator not have run or scored an arm.
evidence: ERS-002 canonical_text: 'followed by blind adjudication against a union, an independent review, and landing through a ledger'. ERS-013 canonical_text and acceptance_criteria never mention blinding; its strongest rule is 'An adjudicator that ran or scored an arm of the same topic may not adjudicate it.' The evidence shard's continuation4/adjudication/README row establishes 'Review-arm recall at 40 and 160 responses per job, the proper-subset result, admissions as the bound, candidate discipline, the same-family disclosure and the source-verified code fact' - no blinding.
suggested_repair: Either drop 'blind' from ERS-002 or add the blinding obligation to ERS-013 with the run that exercised it.

claim: The atom's exact stage-name tokens 'reconcile' and 'compare' are not carried into ERS-002, which renames the stages 'reconciliation' and 'comparison'; ERS-012 then reports the same stages as 'reconcile' and 'compare', so the owner document names its own pipeline stages two ways.
evidence: atom-external-research-owner-canon exact_tokens: ['discovery','implementation','history','reconcile','compare',...]. ERS-002 canonical_text: 'discovery from the product brief, implementation study, history study, reconciliation against the frozen plans snapshot, and comparison producing findings'; its preserved_exact_tokens nonetheless declares ['discovery','implementation','history','reconcile','compare',...]. ERS-012 canonical_text: 'discovery 595.1 s, implementation 1,889.2 s, history 2,079.6 s, reconcile 3,699.3 s and compare 658.3 s'.
suggested_repair: Use the five atom stage tokens verbatim as the stage names in ERS-002 and keep the prose descriptions as gloss.

claim: The atom's exact token 'unsupported or already-covered' appears nowhere in the compiled prose, and the four class names are spelled three different ways across ERS-004, ERS-005/ERS-007 and ACD-467, which a closed contract record shape cannot encode.
evidence: Atom exact_tokens contains 'unsupported or already-covered'. ERS-004 canonical_text writes 'unsupported_or_covered', its negative_constraints write 'unsupported-or-covered', and its preserved_exact_tokens declares 'unsupported or already-covered' although that string is absent from the unit text. Likewise ERS-004 canonical_text says 'product choice', its acceptance_criteria say 'product_choice', and ACD-467 says 'product-choice'.
suggested_repair: Fix one wire spelling per class in ERS-004, carry the atom token as the prose name, and make ERS-005, ERS-007 and ACD-467 use it.

claim: ERS-008 makes the retained unresolved charge count against the cap unconditionally, while ERS-009 and SSYS-037 make that a user-chosen disposition; as drafted the canon both mandates and makes optional the same admission behaviour.
evidence: ERS-008: 'a terminal job that produced no complete native accounting retains its cold allowance as a separate unresolved charge that counts against the cap indefinitely', and its acceptance criterion 'Admission compares captured usage plus in-flight allowance plus unresolved charges against the lifetime cap before every model request.' ERS-009: 'and whether unresolved usage blocks further admission or only stays visible'. SSYS-037: 'an unresolved-usage disposition of blocks_admission or visible_only'.
suggested_repair: State in ERS-008 that the unresolved charge is always retained and reported and that the disposition governs only whether it is added to the admission comparison.

claim: ERS-009 and SSYS-037 both assign the defaults for the four limits to External Research, but no unit states a default for any of them, so the obligation is asserted and never discharged.
evidence: ERS-009: 'this owner fixes their meaning, their defaults and the rule that a job reports which limit ended it'; SSYS-037: 'Their meaning, their defaults and the rule that every job reports which limit ended it belong to Plans/External_Research.md'. No ERS unit names a cost cap, response ceiling, wall-second limit or lifetime cap value, although the evidence shard records cost-policy.json as establishing 'per-job 40 responses and 2,400 seconds, lifetime caps'.
suggested_repair: Either state the defaults in ERS-009 citing continuation3/gate/cost-policy.json, or record an open question deferring them and drop the claim that this owner already fixes them.

claim: ERS-010 and ERS-011 state opposite conclusions about whether review arms differ in kind, and each uses its conclusion to justify its own stage.
evidence: ERS-010: 'because on identical inputs review models differ in depth rather than in kind and a turn-capped arm reports a ceiling, not a judgement'. ERS-011: 'so the review arms differ in depth and, at the margin, in kind' - supported there by 'one of the three, at 0.82 dollars, held three findings no other review arm reached'.
suggested_repair: Reword ERS-010 to the result it actually rests on - the same model under two ceilings produced a proper subset - and let ERS-011 own the cross-model finding.

claim: ERS-010 states a general cross-model premise and a list of control invariants that the cited run does not establish, which is the generalization the owner atom and the authorization forbid.
evidence: ERS-010: 'on identical inputs review models differ in depth rather than in kind' and 'its own control - identical inputs, model, effort, admissions, workers and batching at a 160-response ceiling'. The evidence shard's ERS-010 bullet establishes only 'an arm capped at 40 responses per job stopped 11 of 12 jobs at the ceiling and reached 18 of 110; its control at 160 responses finished all 12 ... and reached 45, and the capped arm's set is a proper subset of the control's' - one model against its own control, and no invariant list. Atom negative constraint: 'Do not quote a turn-capped arm's recall as a model result or generalize one frozen case into a ranking.' Authorization: 'nothing may be promised that the experiments did not exercise'.
suggested_repair: Attribute the depth-not-kind statement to the one capped-versus-control comparison on one frozen case, and drop the control-invariant list unless continuation 4 records it.

claim: ERS-011 compares captured cost across review arms without naming the per-job ceiling each arm ran under, which is the comparison ERS-010's negative constraint forbids.
evidence: ERS-011: 'three cheap review arms reached 34, 36 and 40 of the 110-finding union for 0.53, 0.82 and 0.16 US dollars of captured usage, against 82.52 dollars for the uncapped strong arm's 45'. ERS-010 negative constraint: 'Do not compare cost or duration across arms that ran under different ceilings.' Neither the unit nor the evidence shard states the cheap arms' ceilings, and ERS-010 describes the same 45-finding arm as a control 'at a 160-response ceiling' while ERS-011 calls it 'the uncapped strong arm'.
suggested_repair: Name each cheap arm's per-job ceiling beside its cost, and use one description of the 45-finding arm across ERS-010 and ERS-011.

claim: The per-stage figures ERS-012 carries into canon cannot all be true as labelled: they are given without saying whether each is a wall span or summed job time, and under either reading they contradict another figure in the same sentence.
evidence: ERS-012: 'ran in 6,378.3 seconds of wall time ... with discovery 595.1 s, implementation 1,889.2 s, history 2,079.6 s, reconcile 3,699.3 s and compare 658.3 s; its three reconcile jobs were cut at the 2,400-second per-job limit.' The five stage figures sum to 8,921.5 s, more than the 6,378.3 s run wall, which is impossible for sequential stage wall spans under ERS-002's 'runs five research stages in order'; read instead as summed job time, reconcile's 3,699.3 s is less than three jobs of 2,400 s. The same unit requires 'the admission-to-terminal wall span, the summed job execution time including retries, and the average concurrency' per stage, and the evidence shard's continuation4/README row establishes all three separately.
suggested_repair: Label each carried stage figure as wall span or summed job time from continuation4/README and restate the set so the arithmetic holds.

claim: ERS-012's first acceptance criterion asserts the 60-to-75-minute target as a satisfied criterion, although the only measured run in the same unit took 1 hour 46 minutes and no unit says the target is unmet.
evidence: Acceptance criterion: 'The per-topic target is 60 to 75 minutes with two to four concurrent agents', against the unit's own 'ran in 6,378.3 seconds of wall time - 1 hour 46 minutes - at an average concurrency of 2.620'. q-002 records the target only as standing: 'until then the target stands as Jared's product target'.
suggested_repair: Make the acceptance criterion about reporting against the target and state in the unit that no measured run has met it yet.

claim: The atom's exact token 'protocol fingerprint' is declared preserved by ERS-014 but never written in its text, which uses 'protocol freeze hash' and a bare 'fingerprint' instead.
evidence: Atom exact_tokens: 'protocol fingerprint'. ERS-014 canonical_text: 'The run manifest pins the protocol freeze hash and the hash of every protocol file the run validated against, so two runs sharing a fingerprint provably ran identical code'; preserved_exact_tokens: ['protocol fingerprint','runtime identity','output manifest','quiesce'] - and 'output manifest' is likewise absent, the text saying 'SHA-256 manifest'.
suggested_repair: Name the recomputable value 'protocol fingerprint' in ERS-014 and use 'output manifest' for the frozen tree manifest.

claim: The owner atom's third negative constraint, that nothing be promised which the campaign did not exercise, is carried by no unit; only three narrow per-unit variants exist, so the owner document has no general rule that every figure names its run.
evidence: atom-external-research-owner-canon negative_constraints: 'Do not promise a stage, bound or figure the September 2026 campaign did not exercise.' No ERS unit carries it; the nearest are ERS-010's 'Do not generalize a single frozen case into a model ranking', ERS-011's 'Do not present one frozen case's cheap-arm recall as a general equivalence' and ERS-012's 'Do not present one run's stage timings as a general performance claim'. The authorization shard states the rule generally: 'nothing may be promised that the experiments did not exercise, and ... every promise cites the run that established it.'
suggested_repair: Add the atom's constraint and the run-citation rule to ERS-001, where the owner's scope is fixed.

claim: The contract-family atom's constraint confining the scripts edit to registration is not carried into ATS-054, so nothing in canon holds a future change to the registration-only boundary the authorization set, even though this wave does edit the verifier.
evidence: atom-external-research-contract-family negative_constraints includes 'Do not change any behaviour of the contracts verifier beyond registering this pair'; ATS-054's negative_constraints are the two other atom constraints plus 'Do not convert static validation into execution evidence or a readiness unlock' and 'Do not restore a literal CONTRACT_PAIRS cardinality to this gate registration'. Authorization: 'added to the contracts verifier's pack list ... as a registration-only scripts edit'; dec-002 records 'raising the authored cardinality from 30 to 31'.
suggested_repair: Add the atom's registration-only constraint verbatim to ATS-054's negative_constraints.

claim: Plans/Automated_Testing_System.md is edited by this compile but is not in the authorization shard's list of admitted scope, and no decision record admits it.
evidence: authorization.md 'Scope admitted by this authorization' lists the owner document Plans/External_Research.md, the contracts pair plus the registration-only scripts edit, 'consumer references in Plans/assistant-chat-design.md, Plans/Planning_Ledger_System.md and Plans/Settings_System.md', and this ledger - Plans/Automated_Testing_System.md appears nowhere. compile_queue.json nonetheless lists it in canonical_plan_targets, compiled_owner_docs and compiled_plan_outputs, and dec-002's approval_basis covers only the verifier pack-list registration.
suggested_repair: Cite the brief passage that admits the Automated_Testing_System edit in the authorization shard, or add a decision record admitting ATS-054 as a fourth consumer reference.

claim: PLS-023 declares 'standing repair authorization' as a preserved exact token, as its atom requires, but never uses the phrase and never says that a correction lands under that authorization.
evidence: atom-research-landing-ledger-consumer exact_tokens: ['standing repair authorization','currentness','independent review','ledger question record']. PLS-023 preserved_exact_tokens repeats the first three, but its text says only 'The ledger records the landing; it does not authorize it, because a correction still requires its currentness re-check and independent review and a capability or product choice still requires the user's recorded answer.'
suggested_repair: Say in PLS-023 that a correction lands under the standing repair authorization, which the ledger records and does not confer.

claim: SSYS-037 defers the four settings inventory rows to 'the authorized inventory wave', but nothing in the packet authorizes such a wave and no open question or remaining_work item tracks the deferred rows, so the obligation leaves the ledger untracked.
evidence: SSYS-037: 'The rows themselves are added to Plans/settings_inventory.json in the authorized inventory wave; this unit fixes ownership and meaning and claims no existing row.' dec-005 only says 'adding settings inventory rows is not in this wave's scope'. authorization.md names no inventory wave, and open_items.json lists q-001 to q-004 with no item for the rows.
suggested_repair: Open a ledger question for the settings inventory rows naming their owner, or cite the record that authorizes the inventory wave.

claim: ACD-467, PLS-023 and ATS-054 are drafted as bare YAML blocks with no '### <id> - <title>' heading and no ContractRef line, while every other unit in the same compile has both.
evidence: ACD-467, PLS-023 and ATS-054 draft_text each begin with '```yaml' and end at the closing fence. ERS-001 to ERS-014 begin '### ERS-0NN - <Title>' and end 'ContractRef: ContractName:...', and SSYS-037 has a '### SSYS-037 - External Research Limit Values' heading, prose and a ContractRef line.
suggested_repair: Give the three appended consumer units the same heading, prose lead and ContractRef line the rest of the compile uses.

claim: Three units cite experiment documents with the '/mnt/Cursor' prefix stripped, so the source_lineage entries read as repository-relative paths that do not exist in the repository.
evidence: ERS-010 and ERS-013 source_lineage: 'PM-Experiments/research-audit-native-20260907/process-pilot-20260908/REVIEW_ADJUDICATION_20260916.md'; ERS-012 source_lineage: 'PM-Experiments/research-audit-native-20260907/process-pilot-20260908/BRIEF_GOAL3_RESEARCH_CANON_20260917.md'. Both shards cite them absolutely: authorization.md 'Source: /mnt/Cursor/PM-Experiments/research-audit-native-20260907/process-pilot-20260908/BRIEF_GOAL3_RESEARCH_CANON_20260917.md' and the evidence table row '/mnt/Cursor/PM-Experiments/.../REVIEW_ADJUDICATION_20260916.md'.
suggested_repair: Restore the absolute /mnt/Cursor prefix in the source_lineage entries of ERS-010, ERS-012 and ERS-013.

claim: ERS-010 and ERS-013 rest on a source the evidence shard itself flags as still being appended to, and neither unit nor any ledger record repeats that its hash is a snapshot rather than a frozen file.
evidence: evidence.md row: 'REVIEW_ADJUDICATION_20260916.md (appended to after this reading; the hash is the 2026-09-17 snapshot, not a frozen file)'. ERS-013 and ERS-010 list it in source_lineage with no such qualifier, while ERS-014 requires that provenance rest on quiesced, hashed, frozen trees.
suggested_repair: Carry the 'snapshot, not frozen' qualifier into the units that cite it, or freeze a copy and cite that.

claim: Five units declare preserved_exact_tokens that their own text does not contain, so the field cannot be used to check that this compile preserved what it claims.
evidence: ERS-005 declares 'Deny with changes' and 'Ask a question' but deliberately does not restate the response set; ERS-007 declares 'accepted for planning' and 'unapproved optional capability', neither of which appears (its text says 'a deferred or unapproved item'); ERS-008 declares 'native records' against text reading 'native usage records'; ERS-009 declares 'bound_by' against 'names the limit that bound it'; ERS-013 declares 'same family' against 'shares a model family'.
suggested_repair: Reduce each preserved_exact_tokens list to strings the unit actually contains, or adjust the wording so the declared token is present.

claim: Four of the five defects the evidence shard attributes to continuation4/corrections.json are carried into canon; the shared temp-file name is carried by no unit.
evidence: evidence.md row for 'continuation4/corrections.json': 'The stream-block response count, the post-response boundary defect, the shared temp-file name, the hardcoded runtime version, and the 41-against-40 reading'. ERS-008 carries the first two, ERS-014 the hardcoded runtime version ('never declared'), ERS-009 the 41-against-40 reading ('at most N admitted with one response possibly already in flight'); no unit mentions per-job temp-file isolation.
suggested_repair: Add a per-job artifact-isolation obligation to ERS-014 or ERS-002, or record why the defect needs no canon.

claim: ERS-006 and PLS-023 require an independent review recorded with the commit it reviewed, but no ledger state record names a commit or branch head for this wave, so the review verdict has nothing to attach to.
evidence: ERS-006: 'an independent review by an agent that ran no research job and scored no arm, whose verdict is recorded with the commit it reviewed'. compile_queue.json records 'latest_audit_ref': 'reports/external-research-canon-20260917/verification.json' and 'latest_audit_status': '...PASS_PENDING_INDEPENDENT_BRANCH_REVIEW' with no commit id, and the audit ref carries no SHA-256 although the authorization requires 'every source cited by path and SHA-256'.
suggested_repair: Record the reviewed commit and the verification bundle's SHA-256 in compile_queue.json before the review verdict is filed.

claim: compiled_plan_outputs omits the derived shard and index files this branch regenerates, which q-004 says it does, so the ledger's own output list is incomplete.
evidence: compile_queue.json compiled_plan_outputs lists 'Plans/00-plans-index.md', 'Plans/sharding_config.json', the five owner documents, the two contract files and 'scripts/pm-new-contracts-verify.py' - no Plans/_shards/** or Plans/.plan_index/**, while q-004's detail says the two branches share 'the six Plans/.plan_index files that both regenerate' and validation_state reports 'plan_index': 'pass', 'configured_shards': 'pass'. Plans/ledgers/v2/ledger_registry.json, named in q-004 as a conflicting changed path, is likewise absent.
suggested_repair: List the regenerated Plans/_shards/**, Plans/.plan_index/** and the ledger registry in compiled_plan_outputs.

claim: Two dependency enumerations inside the owner document disagree with the units they name.
evidence: ERS-008 declares 'depends_on: [ERS-002]' but ERS-002 declares 'unblocks: [ERS-003, ERS-004, ERS-012]'; ERS-003 declares 'unblocks: [ERS-004, ERS-013, ERS-014]' but ERS-013 declares 'depends_on: [ERS-004, ERS-010]'. ERS-001 by contrast enumerates all thirteen dependents, so the field is meant to be complete.
suggested_repair: Add ERS-008 to ERS-002's unblocks and either add ERS-003 to ERS-013's depends_on or drop ERS-013 from ERS-003's unblocks.
